description:
Found s393 while diagnosing #315 (uni/parser.t's first row, `is *tèst,
"*main::tèst"`).

REPRODUCER (both lines wrong; the second shows it is NOT a Unicode issue):

    use utf8;
    print *tèst, "\n";     # perl: *main::tèst    PCL: *MAIN::TÈST
    print *plain, "\n";    # perl: *main::plain   PCL: *MAIN::PLAIN

CAUSE: a glob stringifies through the CL symbol's name, and single-segment
package names are upcased into CL packages (that is the load-time convention),
so both the package part and the name part come back upcased.  PCL ALREADY
carries the original-case package name out of band for `caller()` — see
docs/caller-implementation.md — and the glob printer does not consult it.  The
NAME part needs the same treatment: the emitter knows the perl spelling.

COST MEASURED: uni/parser.t 3 rows (its first row is the sanity check, so the
file's later rows may also be blocked by it — re-measure after the fix).
Probably wider: anything that prints a glob or compares one to a string.

BAR: probe both spellings vs perl (ASCII and Unicode), plus a glob in a
non-main package and a glob slot (`*FH{IO}`); corpus-diff; gate; and re-measure
uni/parser.t, splicing its snapshot row with the cause.

=== DONE s395d.  Both halves of a glob stringification now undo their case inversion; the package half through a new %pcl-cl-pkg-to-perl-name (the exact inverse of perl-pkg-to-cl-pkg-name), because inverting unconditionally would upcase an all-lowercase MULTI-segment package (version::regex).  The *FOO{PACKAGE} slot was fixed with it.  uni/parser.t 17 -> 23 ok.  Guard: 3 rows in Pl/t/local-glob-01.t.  Probed vs perl: *plain, *Foo::bar, *STDOUT, *main::x, a multi-segment lowercase package, {NAME}/{PACKAGE}, and \*plain being a GLOB ref.
subject: Glob stringification is UPCASED: `print *plain` gives *MAIN::PLAIN, perl gives *main::plain
